intervals.label: Phase I apparatus (University of Washington)
intervals.note: R&D/demonstration apparatus, not a mature physics detector. Start is the year the collaboration first demonstrated CRES (official About page: Phase I demonstrated CRES on Kr-83m); construction predates it and is not sourced.
intervals.quote: Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES), which was first demonstrated by the collaboration in 2014 ... Phase I in our science program was to demonstrate the feasibility of CRES on single electrons emitted from a gaseous source, Krypton-83m.

name: Project 8 CRES apparatus
notes: facility:university-of-washington-cenpa was a dangling reference for most of this session (owned by the 'axions' lead) but has since been created (also hosting ADMX); site:uw-cenpa-campus (a geocoder-derived campus point, kind: campus) now exists too, so the placement below references it directly rather than guessing a slug.

placements.locator: DOE Office of Science highlight 2015-11 (location); Project 8 About page (2014 first demonstration)
placements.note: site:uw-cenpa-campus is a campus-level marker (owned by the 'axions' lead); the Phase I apparatus's own building/room is not separately sourced. Start 2014 is the year CRES was first demonstrated by the collaboration (official About page); the University of Washington location comes from the DOE Office of Science highlight (2015), so the start is an upper bound.
placements.quote: constructed a prototype instrument at the University of Washington to demonstrate a new electron spectroscopy technique

magnetic_field.note: Field of the Phase I apparatus per the DOE Office of Science highlight (2015). The later Phase II apparatus used 0.959 T (arXiv:2503.08807).
magnetic_field.quote: microwave signal of tritium endpoint electrons in a 1-Tesla magnetic field

summary.plain: A small tabletop instrument built at the University of Washington that catches the faint radio hum a single electron makes as it spirals in a magnetic field, the first step toward weighing the neutrino this way.
summary.technical: Project 8 Phase I CRES apparatus: single-electron cyclotron-radiation detection cell in a ~1 T magnetic field, demonstrated on 83mKr conversion electrons at the University of Washington (CRES first demonstrated in 2014); later phases add gaseous tritium sources.

technology.locator: Project 8 Phase II apparatus paper, abstract
technology.quote: Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES) is a novel technique for the precise measurement of relativistic electron energy.
technology.value: Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES): single-electron microwave radiometry in a magnetic trap
